newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down on strong May output, Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down on strong May output, Sakakibara.

text.p: The key September futures JGB contract ended lower on Tuesday due to strong 4.5 percent month-on-month growth in revised May industrial output, traders said.
The JGBs also fell on a foreign media report that newly appointed MOF Vice Minister Eisuke Sakakibara said market views on the economy are still too pessimistic.

Jiro Ushio, chairman of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives, said the dollar may rise to 140 yen if Japan's structural reform effort fails. Some said this also triggered light selling as it re-ignited rate rise fears.
The key September closed at 124.75, near the day's low of 124.73, compared with Monday's 124.96.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.310 percent at 0640 GMT, up from Monday's 2.280 percent.
Adding to the bearish sentiment was news that the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan (LTCB) had signed a letter of intent to form a global strategic alliance with Swiss Bank Corp.

"The LTCB-SBC news suggested there would be one less bad factor for Japan's ailing banking sector, which may give some room for the Bank of Japan to prepare for a credit tightening," said a European bank trader.
Some traders said LTCB has been speculated to be withdrawing part of its overseas operations, including its London branch.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, interest rates rose across the spectrum. The three-year IRS was at 1.44/48 percent at 0706 GMT, compared with Monday's 1.40/44 percent.
There was some action in over-the-counter JGB options market, traders said.
Some said a foreign operator bought put options in recently issued 10-year JGBs in large lot.
